definitions.explanation: A person who has been legally adopted into a family. In Japan, adoption has historically been used not only for children but also for adults, particularly to bring a capable son-in-law into a family to carry on the family name and business.

examples.english: He was given up for adoption.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもがいない⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{養子|ようし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}えた→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧。
examples.english: A childless couple adopted a child.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家業|かぎょう}→家業：12353_kagyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{継|つ}がせる→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{成人|せいじん}→成人：03378_seijin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{男性|だんせい}→男性：01655_dansei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{養子|ようし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{歴史的|れきしてき}→歴史的：05671_rekishiteki⟧にあった。
examples.english: In Japan, there was historically a custom of adopting adult men to carry on the family business.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese {養子|ようし}{縁組|えんぐみ} (adoption) is distinctive because it includes adult adoption, which is still practiced today. Companies and families without male heirs may adopt a son-in-law ({婿|むこ}{養子|ようし}), who takes the family name and inherits the family business. Japan has one of the highest rates of adult adoption in the world.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {養子|ようし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to give up for adoption)
- {養子|ようし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧ (to adopt; to welcome as an adopted child)
- {養子|ようし}{縁組|えんぐみ} (adoption arrangement)
- {婿|むこ}{養子|ようし} (adopted son-in-law)
- {養子|ようし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to adopt)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {養子|ようし}: adopted child (legal adoption)
- {里子|さとご}: foster child (foster care, not permanent adoption)
- ⟦{養親|ようしん}→養親：16814_youshin⟧: adoptive parent
